answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slashable web-of-trust bonds: a new agent locks a stake and needs three unrelated, already-bonded agents to vouch for it, with each voucher jointly liable, so if an account proves to be a clone its endorsers lose collateral. The attacker must then buy many genuinely distinct bonded identities or bribe existing ones, paying capital plus the risk of being slashed. Trust accrues slowly like a pearl; a comet of fake identities flares and vanishes, while a mesa of rented accounts crumbles the moment one voucher defaults.
